title: Physical interpretation: strong binding and Coulomb repulsion
html:
Remark. Physical interpretation: strong binding and Coulomb repulsion

The decomposition separates crossing energy into two channels.

Channel identification.

Channel Weight per crossing Under crossing reversal Physical force
Symmetric \pm\cosh(\ln q), signed by the crossing negates Strong binding
Antisymmetric +\sinh(\ln q), independent of the crossing sign fixed Coulomb (electromagnetic)

The symmetric part binds regardless of charge. The antisymmetric part distinguishes charges. The sign-blindness of the \sinh weight is what leaves a residue when a composite is paired with its mirror, and is the reason the two channel totals carry the multiplicities p - m and p + m respectively (decomposition).

Pair creation.

When creating an e^- e^+ pair, cancellation yields:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(e^-) + \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(e^+)
  = 6\sinh(\ln q)
  \approx 0.630 \quad (\text{Skein units}).

Symmetric contributions cancel. The residual 6\sinh\lambda > 0 yields pure Coulomb repulsion, separating the pair.

Channel ratio.

At q = q_0, for a positive braid closure (ratio identity):

  \frac{E_{\mathrm{asym}}}{E_{\mathrm{sym}}} = \tanh(\ln q_0) \approx 0.104.

The antisymmetric channel carries roughly 10\% of the symmetric channel's magnitude. This is a ratio of the two channel weights at the substrate anchor, not a running coupling ratio: no renormalisation scale is attached to it, and it should not be read as a value of \alpha / \alpha_s, which varies over the accessible energy range. The electromagnetic coupling proper is obtained from the antisymmetric eigenvalue by the EM coupling projection.

Crossing energy table for a particle with n_c positive crossings:

Quantity Formula T_{2,3} (n_c = 3) Value
Total energy n_cq 3q 3.330
Strong component n_c\cosh(\ln q) 3\cosh(\ln q) 3.015
Coulomb component n_c\sinh(\ln q) 3\sinh(\ln q) 0.315
Pair net energy n_c(q - q^{-1}) 3(q - q^{-1}) 0.630
Channel ratio \tanh(\ln q) \tanh(\ln q) 0.104

By Hopf stability, \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p}) < 0. The strong symmetric channel dominates the Coulomb antisymmetric channel, ensuring proton stability.
